transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Julia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Lead ML Eng, Acme Insights), Tom Benton (Platform Eng Manager), Luis Ortega (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery to map integration surface area. Focus: whether Acme should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated reservation, or Private VPC; gateway/proxy vs sidecar patterns for request routing; SDK and LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility; rate limits/quotas; observability hooks and tracing.

Topics covered: integration architecture, SDK usage, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy vs sidecar, rate limit patterns, telemetry & tracing hooks, security/KMS, POC next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Julia Park: hey everyone thanks for making time today, I'll kick us off. this is Julia from Redwood, AE, and with me is Marcus our SE. 
[00:10] Priya Sharma: hey all, Priya here. quick heads up, i'm on a slightly noisy call but i'll mute when not talking. 
[00:15] Tom Benton: Tom here. short agenda from our side, we want to understand integration effort and where to put the gateway. 
[00:22] Marcus Reed: awesome, thanks Tom. real quick, can you share a bit about your current stack and how you call LLMs today?
[00:28] Priya Sharma: sure. we have a java-based microservice platform on k8s, internal gateway using envoy, we proxy most external APIs through an api-gateway. right now we're using a mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and a self-hosted smaller model for cheaper chats — we call it, uh, a local llama variant. traffic peaks ~650 rps auth requests, gen calls maybe 120 rps, average prompt length 220 tokens, completions avg 120 tokens.
[01:05] Julia Park: got it. curious — what's most important: latency tail, cost predictability, or data residency?
[01:12] Luis Ortega: latency first for product features, predictability second, and we also have some strict retention rules for PII so data residency matters for some customers.
[01:21] Marcus Reed: thanks. that aligns with the typical tradeoffs. we generally recommend Hosted for quick start, Dedicated when you need predictable throughput and isolation, and Private VPC if you need customer-managed networking or airgap. in your case latency + residency might push you toward Dedicated or Private.
[01:37] Tom Benton: one thing we debated internally — run a central gateway that routes requests to Redwood hosted endpoints or run a sidecar next to services that call Redwood directly. pros/cons?
[01:47] Julia Park: fair question. gateway centralizes auth, rate-limiting, and observability and makes canarying easier; sidecar gives you lower cross-network hops and isolates per-service config. with Dedicated you can also reduce cross-region hops by pinning model instances.
[02:00] Priya Sharma: so if we do sidecar, would we use Redwood SDK in the sidecar and then envoy to do mTLS to redwood? or do you prefer using a central proxy that handles token rotation?
[02:10] Marcus Reed: both are valid. sidecar pattern: embed the Redwood SDK (we have java and python SDKs) in the sidecar and maintain local KV cache for frequently used prefixes — saves a token call. central gateway pattern: gateway performs batching and caching centrally; easier quota enforcement and audit logging. central also reduces SDK rollout work.
[02:34] Tom Benton: what's the amount of effort to wire up the SDK? we use LangChain and some LlamaIndex helpers in python for analytics pipelines.
[02:42] Marcus Reed: our SDKs are light — a few lines to swap the base client; we also provide LangChain/LLamaIndex connectors. quick example: in python you can swap the Redwood client into your existing chain with a custom llm wrapper, and LlamaIndex documents work with our embeddings endpoint with minimal changes. we can share example snippets.
[02:59] Priya Sharma: snippet sharing would help. also curious about long-running chat state: can Redwood host KV cache for session tokens or do we need to provide?
[03:10] Julia Park: Dedicated includes optional KV cache co-located with the runtime; Hosted has prefix caching too but you can opt for sticky routing to preserve KV across requests. Private/On-prem gives you full control. if you need strict residency, Private is the way.
[03:28] Tom Benton: what about rate limits — we have per-tenant quotas and global burst allowances. can Redwood enforce per-API-key quotas?
[03:36] Marcus Reed: yes. per-token or per-route quotas are supported in the console and via API. you can set rate limits by API key, route, or blame group. we also support burst tokens and token buckets. for Dedicated we can model your tenancy and expose quota metrics to your dashboard.
[03:52] Priya Sharma: prometheus metrics? tracing? we use datadog + open telemetry.
[03:57] Marcus Reed: we emit metrics and traces. we have Prometheus-compatible metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and request-level logs you can stream to a s3/bucket or forward to Datadog. the console also surfaces per-token cost and latency breakdowns.
[04:12] Luis Ortega: any gotchas when using our existing envoy layer? we don't want double-rate-limiting or conflicting timeouts.
[04:18] Julia Park: from experience, the main gotcha is timeout misconfiguration — you want the gateway timeout slightly longer than the client so you don't cut the trace. and ensure envoy's retry policies don't cause duplicate model calls; we can provide recommended envoy config to prevent retries for non-idempotent endpoints.
[04:36] Tom Benton: can we host a small gateway in our VPC that calls Redwood hosted endpoints over private link?
[04:42] Marcus Reed: yes, we support private link peering for Hosted, or you can run our Private control plane in your VPC. both approaches reduce public egress.
[04:52] Priya Sharma: security — KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SSO?
[04:57] Julia Park: we integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for Dedicated/Private. Hosted offers envelope encryption with managed keys but we can bring-your-own-key for Dedicated in many contracts. we have SOC2 and ISO certs — i'll attach the packet. SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC at token and route level.
[05:15] Tom Benton: great. if we go Dedicated, how does autoscaling work — we're worried about cost with spiky traffic.
[05:22] Marcus Reed: Dedicated has autoscaling policies and burst pools. you pick baseline reserved capacity and autoscale rules; we also support rate-based scaling to cover bursts without massive reserved commit. Optimize engine suggests batching and quantization profiles to reduce token costs.
[05:36] Priya Sharma: you mentioned batching — is there a way to do client-side batching in our gateway to reduce token cost but maintain latency SLOs?
[05:43] Marcus Reed: yes, Redwood SDK supports async batching primitives. plus we do continuous batching server-side to optimize GPU throughput. the trick is setting max wait window vs latency percentile; we can help simulate tradeoffs for your distribution.
[05:58] Luis Ortega: one more architectural question — would you recommend a proxy that rewrites prompts for PII stripping before sending? we want to mask PII client-side.
[06:07] Julia Park: PII stripping is typically best at the gateway/sidecar boundary before crossing service boundaries. you can also use our pre-processing hooks and redactors. for regulatory reasons some customers do both: sidecar scrubs then proxy enforces policy.
[06:26] Priya Sharma: switching gears — LangChain & LlamaIndex. we use both in experimental pipelines. any limitations?
[06:33] Marcus Reed: no big limitations. our connectors expose the completions and embeddings APIs. for LangChain, you can plug the Redwood LLM class into chains and for LlamaIndex we supply an embeddings adapter and a simple document store integration. performance wise the latency is driven by model choice and sequence lengths. in POC we usually test a couple models and quantizations to find the sweet spot.
[06:54] Tom Benton: what about model fallbacks — if the Dedicated pool gets saturated can we route to a degraded cheaper model automatically?
[07:01] Julia Park: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies by model family, region, or tier. you can define canary percent and automatic fallback in the route config. we also support A/B testing and rollbacks.
[07:12] Priya Sharma: ok that's useful. cost control — can the console show token-level spend by route or by API key?
[07:19] Marcus Reed: yes, token-level cost breakdowns by token type, route, and customer can be drilled into. we can add tagging so you can slice spend by service or team.
[07:29] Tom Benton: do you have a recommended pattern for per-customer quotas and overage handling?
[07:34] Julia Park: typically: a soft quota with webhooks on breach, then throttle to a lower tier, and finally hard reject. the webhooks let you notify customers or trigger micropay. we can demonstrate the webhook config in the console.
[07:48] Priya Sharma: curious about retry semantics: if our gateway retries and the model executed once, we could double-bill. how do you advise handling idempotency?
[07:57] Marcus Reed: include an idempotency key per user prompt; our API supports idempotency and deduplication windows. for non-idempotent ops, avoid automatic retries at the gateway level. we'll share a recommended pattern.
[08:12] Tom Benton: could you show a quick sample of the SDK usage and a LangChain adapter?
[08:17] Marcus Reed: sure, i'll paste links after. short pseudo: 'from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., region=...); response = client.generate(prompt)' — for LangChain you wrap that in an LLM class. we'll send code samples.
[08:33] Priya Sharma: do you have an official LlamaIndex connector for embeddings batching? we've had to patch things in the past.
[08:39] Marcus Reed: yes, we have an embeddings adapter that supports batch embeddings and automatic backpressure. it's in our python SDK repo. we'll share the link.
[08:48] Luis Ortega: observability hooks — can we get per-request trace ids so it ties back to our end-to-end trace?
[08:53] Marcus Reed: yes, we propagate trace ids if you send them (we honor W3C traceparent headers). we also annotate traces with model, sequence length, and token counters. logs can be forwarded to your log sink.
[09:06] Tom Benton: are there any known issues with LlamaIndex or LangChain versions? we are on langchain 0.0.#### (slight mess)
[09:14] Marcus Reed: occasionally adapter code lags major LangChain refactors; we maintain compatibility tests and patch quickly but for POC we usually pin to supported versions listed in our sample repo.
[09:24] Priya Sharma: okay, so next steps from our side: we want the recommended envoy config, example sidecar SDK snippet, and an estimation for Dedicated baseline cost given our peak usage.
[09:34] Julia Park: will do. we'll draft a recommended envoy config that disables retries for completions endpoints and sets sensible timeouts. we'll also provide a cost estimator for Dedicated with baseline reservations and autoscale.
[09:44] Luis Ortega: timeline — we have an external launch in Q2 and need the pilot done by end of feb. doable?
[09:51] Marcus Reed: yes we can run a 4-week POC. week 1: baseline measurements and traffic capture; week 2: POC Dedicated pool and integration (sidecar or gateway); week 3: tuning (batching/cache); week 4: final report and next steps.
[10:06] Priya Sharma: sounds good. do you do benchmark runs with our dataset to verify latency P95 numbers?
[10:12] Marcus Reed: yes, we run controlled bench runs. for Dedicated we can spin up a smaller bench cluster and simulate your token distribution; we'll provide the script.
[10:21] Tom Benton: any legal/procurement blockers we should anticipate for Dedicated?
[10:26] Julia Park: standard SLA/contract, data processing addendum for EU residency, and if you choose Private we need infra access for automated installs; can supply the SOW templates. procurement usually expects security attestation and SOC2 which we provide.
[10:40] Priya Sharma: a few nitty gritty items — websocket streaming for partial generation? we use streaming UI.
[10:46] Marcus Reed: streaming is supported in both Hosted and Dedicated. for Private you have streaming via GRPC or websocket depending on your network policy. streaming latencies are typically lower if you have the runtime in same region or on-prem.
[10:59] Luis Ortega: what's the maintenance window impact for Dedicated? we can't have more than 30m of downtime for critical routes.
[11:05] Julia Park: Dedicated SLAs are configurable; maintenance is typically rolling and you can opt for maintenance windows; we also provide automatic fallback to hosted in cluster maintenance windows if you want zero impact.
[11:20] Tom Benton: OK — can you put together a proposal that includes a 4-week POC with pricing bands and the envoy config?
[11:27] Julia Park: yes i'll send that and the security pack. Marcus will own the bench script and demo setup.
[11:33] Priya Sharma: also please include the LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter code samples and the list of supported SDK versions.
[11:38] Marcus Reed: noted, we'll attach repo links and example notebooks.
[11:43] Tom Benton: last question — during POC, if we hit cost concerns, is there a quick knob to throttle or switch models?
[11:50] Marcus Reed: absolutely, you can set runtime policies: auto-fallback to cheaper model family or apply runtime quantization profiles. you can also limit token-per-minute via quotas while we tune batch windows.
[12:03] Julia Park: ok let's do a quick recap of action items and next steps.
[12:07] Julia Park: Julia: send security packet, envoy recommended config, and Dedicated baseline estimate by Monday 2026-01-18.
[12:15] Marcus Reed: Marcus: bench script and LangChain/LlamaIndex example notebooks by 2026-01-24.
[12:20] Priya Sharma: Priya: collect and share anonymized traffic histograms and top prompt templates by 2026-01-22.
[12:26] Tom Benton: Tom: coordinate internal stakeholders and confirm POC scope by 2026-01-21.
[12:31] Luis Ortega: Luis: review proposal and confirm budget at exec review 2026-01-28.
[12:37] Julia Park: perfect. we'll follow up in email and drop all links. thanks everyone.
[12:41] End of transcript.
